content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to [product_name] and have some questions about program modules. I noticed that the device has a built-in slot for a microSD card. Is it possible to use a microSD card as a transfer card, similar to the way it's done with more advanced [company_name] PLCs—insert the card, move the program, then remove it? Or does it need to remain inserted as a program card? How do the program module and SD card differ in their roles? I appreciate any guidance!

Earlier versions of [product_name] up to and including [article_no] used dedicated program modules for program storage. Beginning with [article_no], the slot supports only standard SD cards, but not MicroSD. From [article_no], the slot is exclusively for MicroSD cards. You can use the SD card to transfer programs. For example, save your program to the SD card on your PC, but ensure it is in the required format and not the usual project file format. The file should have a .bin extension and a specific file name. Use "File > Save as" to save it as "[document].bin". Insert the card into [product_name], power it on, and the program will start.

Thanks [user_name]! I have a non-display [product_name], [product_name] TDE, and a 16GB SDHC card (formatted to FAT32, tried various cluster sizes). Programming via ethernet cable worked successfully, but using the microSD card hasn't. The manual suggests a tab labeled "Card" should appear in the settings, but I only see Program, Setup, Network, and Diagnostics. Diagnostics confirms the microSD card is recognized. Am I missing a step? Could this be due to the microSDHC card format? In previous discussions you mentioned that microSDHC cards can be used ([url]) and also that they cannot ([url]).

I can't give a definitive answer since I haven't tested every card variant. The newer discussion link had more trial experiences, including attempts with SDHC cards. In contrast, the older link pointed to information from the manual, which only specifies SD and doesn't mention SDHC or other formats. Whether [product_name] has a display doesn't matter in this case. If your [product_name] TDE menu is missing the "Stop" option, you're likely in operator mode. Go to "Setup" and select "Change to ADMIN"—press ENTER and enter the default password ([product_name]). This unlocks the extended menu, including "Stop". Once you put [product_name] in STOP mode, you'll then see the "Card" option.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are encountering uncertainty when using microSD features for transferring programs to [product_name] devices, expecting workflows similar to higher-tier PLCs from [company_name]. Confusion arises regarding supported SD formats, file preparation steps, and the activation of card options in the device menu, particularly when not switching to ADMIN mode. Limits in menu access without the correct user mode lead to further user hesitation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are seeking clear information about compatibility between [product_name] devices and microSD cards, easy-to-follow program transfer methods comparable to higher-end PLCs, and straightforward menu navigation for card operations.
